title: In 1812, Cannonballs Bounced Off a Wooden Ship. Here's Why

scenes.text: In 1812, cannonballs bounced off a wooden ship.
The USS Constitution was fighting the British frigate Guerriere on August 19th.
An 18-pound cannonball hit her hull and fell into the sea.
A sailor shouted, huzzah, her sides are made of iron!
They weren't. The hull was thick, layered oak, strong enough to stop many shots.
The fight lasted nearly an hour, and the British ship lost all three masts.
The nickname stuck. She's still Old Ironsides.

description:
On August 19th, 1812, British cannonballs bounced off the hull of the USS Constitution, and a sailor said her sides were made of iron.
The ship has been called Old Ironsides ever since.
Would you have believed it?
first_comment: What is the toughest thing you have ever seen survive a hit?
